subject.title: [Bug]: Memory detection skips macOS (darwin) — os.freemem() / os.totalmem() never reported to agent on non-Linux platforms

question: Should `noteStartupOptimizationHints` target Darwin hosts the same way as Linux, only low-memory Darwin hosts, or remain Linux-only?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the helper and note copy currently describe low-power Linux/Pi/VM guidance; broad Darwin ARM targeting could make normal Apple Silicon Macs see startup-tuning advice that maintainers may or may not want.

options.title: Support Darwin ARM and low-memory
options.body: Treat Linux and Darwin as startup-tune platforms for ARM or <=8 GiB hosts, with platform-neutral wording and Darwin regression tests.

options.title: Support low-memory Darwin only
options.body: Add Darwin only for <=8 GiB hosts to cover Lume/small VM reports while avoiding Apple Silicon high-memory note noise.

options.title: Keep Linux-only
options.body: Document that macOS is intentionally excluded from this startup-tuning hint and close the linked fix attempts as not planned.

recommendation.title: Support Darwin ARM and low-memory
recommendation.body: Treat Linux and Darwin as startup-tune platforms for ARM or <=8 GiB hosts, with platform-neutral wording and Darwin regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the startup optimization helper and Linux-only targeting in the merged startup optimization slice.
